name: id
description: One identity made of many accounts. An Ethereum wallet, a Solana wallet, a Bitcoin address, a Cosmos key, a GitHub login — each proves itself by signing a statement that names the identity it is joining, and the set of them becomes a single id. There is no account table and no password: the identity IS the append-only log of signatures, and `audit` replays it and re-checks every one of them offline. Joining is deliberately two-signature — the account proves it holds its key, and a member proves it consents — because a signature alone would let anyone attach their wallet to somebody else's identity; the consenting signature is copied into the event it authorises, so the log holds a complete chain of who let whom in. Two identities that both already exist become one only when a member of each signs the same pair. Leaving is one-sided: your own signature always removes you. Eleven chains across four signing schemes (EIP-191, Bitcoin's signed-message format, Cosmos ADR-036, raw Ed25519), verified with Keccak-256, RIPEMD-160, secp256k1 recovery, Ed25519, Base58 and Bech32 all implemented in this module — so an identity exported from here can be re-verified on any host with a Python interpreter, no network, and nothing installed, years after the wallet that signed it is gone.
frontend: src/app.py (stdlib — the console at /id on :50651; proxies /id/_api and drives MetaMask and Phantom directly)
state: ~/.mod/id — ids/<id>.jsonl is the identity; index.json, sessions.json and merges.json are caches of it. Public keys, addresses, statements and signatures only. No private key is ever held, asked for, or storable.

idea.identity: a set of accounts, held together by signatures rather than by a row in a table
idea.log: append-only; every membership claim is a signed event that can be re-checked by anyone
idea.index: a cache — `m id/rebuild` regenerates it from the logs, which is the proof that it is one
idea.portability: `export` gives a document with every proof and no secret; `load` re-verifies all of it before writing a byte

rules.join: two signatures — the joining account, and a member consenting (the consenting proof is stored in the event)
rules.genesis: one signature, because the first account of a new identity has nobody to ask
rules.merge: two signatures — one member from each side, on the same canonically ordered pair
rules.leave: your own signature is always enough to remove yourself
rules.evict: only the root account (the one that created the identity) removes somebody else
rules.replay: a statement names the protocol, the operation, the identity, the account, an expiry and a nonce; the nonce is burned on use, and a failed attempt does not burn it

chains.ethereum: EIP-191 personal_sign, key recovered from the signature — covers Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, BNB, Avalanche and every other EVM network as ONE account, because it is one key
chains.bitcoin: the Bitcoin signed-message format; legacy (1…), nested segwit (3…) and native segwit (bc1q…) all verify. Taproot is refused with a reason — BIP-322 is not widely shipped
chains.litecoin: same scheme, its own magic string and version bytes
chains.solana: raw Ed25519 over the statement; the address is the public key
chains.cosmos: ADR-036 Amino JSON sign document; needs the public key sent alongside, because the signature is not recoverable. One key prints under every chain prefix and the equivalents are reported
chains.near: implicit (64-hex) accounts verify completely; a named account proves the key only, and says so
chains.substrate: Polkadot / Kusama / Bittensor SS58, Ed25519 accounts. sr25519 is NOT verified — it needs Schnorrkel, and the module says so rather than pretending

services.note: accounts with no key prove control by publishing a token. Labelled `publication` everywhere, because the proof lasts only as long as the page does
services.github: a public gist — the owner login is taken from GitHub's answer, not from what was typed
services.x: a public post, read through the public embed endpoint
services.dns: a TXT record at _mod-id.<domain>, resolved over DoH so the host needs no resolver
services.web: any URL you can publish to — proves that page, not the whole domain, and says so

crypto.why: verification is the one thing this module cannot be wrong about, and a proof that needs a package installed is a proof that expires when the package does
crypto.pinned_against: eth_hash, eth_keys, eth_account, pynacl and the published BIP-173/BIP-350/RFC-8032 vectors, wherever those are present

endpoints.challenge: POST /challenge {chain, address, op, id, other, name, ttl}
endpoints.verify: POST /verify {chain, address, message, signature} — one-shot, stores nothing

env.ID_HOST: the host name written into every statement (default the machine's)
